title: The Drawer That Counts Footprints
premise: A dresser wants six folded shirts to fit without hiding the bottom ones, but each fold uses a different footprint. A measured toy folding template makes the available drawer layout visible before packing.
hook: Are these shirts too many, or just packed differently?
visible_action: Flat cloth rectangles fold along guides into equal footprints, then stand in a grid inside a transparent drawer.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Consistent dimensions can make storage capacity and visibility easier to reason about.
gate: Use idealized cloth dimensions; real fabrics, drawer clearance, and preferences vary.

style_application.material: Paper silhouettes or original textured objects
style_application.why: Footprints and retrieval paths are legible without perspective distortion.
style_application.check: Verify dimensions, occupied area and the specific retrieval rule.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A drawer layout turns vague tidiness into a visible fit and access problem.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Use accurately sized original silhouettes on an overhead tray. Show why a visually compact layout may obstruct retrieval.
editorial_pick.gate: Check dimensions and the chosen access rule. Present one example, not a universal organizing prescription.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
